text.p: WesterFed Financial Corp said it has agreed to merge with Security Bancorp, located in Billings, forming the largest publicly traded banking company in Montana with $640 million in deposits.
WesterFed is the holding company for Western Federal Savings Bank of Montana and Security Bancorp is the holding company for Security Bank FSB.
WesterFed will likely include two Security officers on its board, including Chief Executive Officer David Jorgenson. The deal is seen closing by the end of 1997's first quarter.

Under the terms of the agreement, Security Bancorp shareholders may choose to receive $30 in cash for each of their common shares, swap their stock for WesterFed shares or choose to receive cash and stock as long as the stock portion were 40 to 45 percent of the deal.

If shareholders choose to swap their stock, the exchange ratio would be $30.00 divided by the average closing price of WesterFed common stock for a 20-trading day period that begins 30 trading days before closing. Other terms apply if the price is at or below $13.05 or at or above $17.50 a share.
Based on WesterFed's common stock price of $15.25 at the end of business on Tuesday and excluding stock options, the merger would have a value of $44 million, WesterFed said.
The merger also is expected to be accretive to earnings per share in the first full fiscal year of combined operations, assuming only modest cost reductions, it said.
